blockworks_home.title: Blockworks
blockworks_home.h1: Building trust in onchain capital markets.

rubric.evidence: TR has 39 numeric counters above the fold but they are static sidebar counts; BW has 52 numeric tiles, 5 are live crypto price ticker + 9 are live financial deltas (24hr DEX volume, App revenue, Blockchain REV, Stablecoin supply, DAT/ETF flows).
TR has 0 articles, 0 podcasts, /digest is archive-only ('Daily digests start today'). BW has news section, 10 podcast shows, 4 research articles on home, named-analyst commentary.
TR has NewsletterCaptureForm component but no Resend wiring per memory; /digest archive empty. BW promotes The Breakdown daily newsletter prominently across home + footer, has subscribe CTAs.

TR's /pricing page is fully spec'd (Free / Pro $19 / Team $49/seat / Enterprise) but no paywall enforced and no homepage CTA pushing to it. BW Research at app.blockworksresearch.com is a full premium product, 5x 'Sign up' CTAs visible, 'Hundreds of features, one subscription'.
TR has zero events. BW promotes Digital Asset Summit 2026, Permissionless conference, Roundtables footer link.
TR has none. BW has Blockworks Advisory as a top-nav item ('Products > Advisory') plus dedicated /advisory route.

TR has /portal/docs API endpoint, public CLI (npx trendingrepo), published MCP server, and a real /portal/docs polish path. BW mentions 'data API' inside Research (gated, harder to evaluate). TR wins this row.

TR H1: 'One live ranking for open-source breakouts.' — descriptive. BW H1: 'Building trust in onchain capital markets.' — mission-grade with verb + market category. BW's 'Decoding crypto and the markets' tone reads institutional.

TR has no /about, no team page, no HQ, BETA badge prominent. BW publishes mission/vision, HQ '133 W 19th St., New York, NY 10011', dedicated /about route, Trust & Ethics page, open positions page, named founders.
Both have ⌘K. TR's sidebar has 8 sections / 31 nav items (deeper IA but more cluttered). BW's top-nav has 8 dropdown groups (cleaner but flatter). Comparable.
TR has zero published industry frameworks. BW has the Token Transparency Framework (presented to SEC), 'Trusted by industry leaders' module, partnerships with exchanges, financial institutions.
Not directly measured at 390px in this pass; assumption based on TR's lighter payload (97KB vs 685KB) and modern Tailwind 4 stack vs BW's heavier image-led hero. Flagged as 'verify next pass'.
TR: 1534ms load, 97KB transfer, 857KB decoded, 4646 DOM nodes. BW: 6525ms load (4.3x slower), 685KB transfer (7x heavier), 1402KB decoded, 2221 DOM nodes (BW has fewer nodes but heavier media).

TR /repo/<owner>/<name> has 11 data loaders + 6 mention synthesizers per repo (cross-source mentions, funding, revenue overlay, star activity, predictions). BW research articles are deep but each is editorial-led, not entity-database-led. TR's data-shape moat is real.

TR's CONSENSUS, BREAKOUTS, and momentum scoring across 8 social sources (HN, Lobsters, Dev.to, Bluesky, Reddit, X, ProductHunt, GitHub) is the unique moat — surfaced in nav with '3X' consensus indicator. BW has internal data composition but not cross-source-agreement as a primary surface.
